header.problem: Support staff paste long tracking URLs into customer chats, where they wrap, break and cannot be counted.
users: Support agents: shorten a link in one step while on a live chat
Support leads: see how often each shared link is opened

goals.purpose: Every link an agent shares fits on one line
goals.advantage: No more broken wrapped URLs in chats
goals.measure: A short link is created in under 1 second

goals.purpose: Leads can see which links customers open
goals.advantage: Help articles get fixed by evidence, not guesswork
goals.measure: Click counts are visible within 5 seconds of a click

principles: One step for the agent: paste, get a link
Nothing is deleted; expiry hides a link, it does not destroy it
Works offline on one machine: no external services

glossary.code: the 6-character key in a short link
glossary.click: one redirect served for a code

limits.text: p95 redirect under 50 ms on one core
limits.why: redirects sit in front of every customer click

limits: One SQLite file; no other datastore

invariants.text: A code, once issued, always resolves to the same URL
invariants.why: links live on in old chats

tags: trust_boundary: the shorten form takes untrusted URLs

requirements.title: Shorten: a URL becomes a short link
requirements.why: Agents need one-line links in chat

acceptance.text: POST /api/links {url} returns 201 {code, short_url} with a 6-character code
POST /api/links with a URL that is not http(s) returns 422 {error: "bad_url"}

requirements.title: Redirect: a short link opens its URL
requirements.why: A short link is useless unless it lands the customer on the page

acceptance.text: GET /<code> returns 302 to the stored URL; an unknown code returns 404

requirements.title: Stats: a lead sees each link's click count
requirements.why: Leads fix the help articles customers actually open

acceptance.text: GET /api/links/<code>/stats returns {clicks}, one more after each redirect

waiting_room: QR code for each short link
